reasons: Classification is correct: Section 11.1 (five-year initial term with 30-day non-renewal notice) and Section 11.2 (breach/insolvency only) give Corio — the licensee/payer on our side — no convenience exit during a multi-year term, which the detection guidance expressly treats as a deviation and which fails the 60–90 day fallback.

The redline is actionable and directionally correct for the customer: it adds a Corio convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid recurring fees, bars any early-termination fee or acceleration, and confirms Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right — tracking the preferred position and model language.
Edit is additive and minimally invasive: Sections 11.1 and 11.2 are left untouched, so no existing bargained term is disturbed.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a false negative from party-name matching; the inserted text plainly grants Corio (the Customer alias here) a convenience termination right.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day fallback.

Minor, non-blocking: the inserted subsection is unnumbered in the rendered output despite the rationale's reference to renumbering existing 11.3 — a clause number ('11.3') should be added on execution. Also, Commerce One's 30-day end-of-term non-renewal right in 11.1 was left intact; acceptable as non-renewal rather than mid-term convenience termination, and consistent with the stated rationale.
